title: Taifa of Arcos
capsule: The Taifa of Arcos de la Frontera (Arcos de la Frontera, Cádiz province) emerged in 1011 as the Caliphate of Córdoba fragmented, ruled by the Berber Jizrunid dynasty (of the Zanata confederation): Muhammad I al-Jazarī founded it, followed by ʿAbdūn ibn Muḥammad (1030–1053) and Muhammad II al-Qāʾim (1053–1068/9). The Abbadid kings of Seville absorbed Arcos between 1068 and 1091; it then passed under Almoravid control after 1101. A brief revival under the Idrisid lord Abū al-Qāsim Ahyal (1143–1145) was extinguished when the Almohad Caliphate conquered the taifa in 1145. Arcos controlled the fertile hill country east of Jerez, its defensive hilltop position over the Guadalete river giving it strategic importance disproportionate to its modest size.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core city of Arcos de la Frontera is unambiguous; the extent of surrounding territory controlled by the taifa at any given point is poorly attested in surviving sources.
